in_arabic.name: بكر

data.cultural_impact: Bakkar is a name that holds considerable importance in the rich cultural history of the Islamic world. For centuries, it has been a popular given name, not just for humans but also for animals in various Islamic communities, particularly in India and Pakistan. The name is most notably associated with holy figures in Islamic tradition, notably Bakr Ibn ‘Abdullah Al-Siddeeq, who was one of the earliest converts to Islam, and the Prophet Muhammad’s (pbuh) respected companion and cousin, Ali ibn Abu Talib (RA), who was also known as Bakr or Tibiah. Aside from historical figures, Bakar is also used as a name for animals such as cows, symbolizing blessings, nurturing, and prosperity.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name 'Bakkar' can be traced back to its origin in the Arabic language. The word 'bakr' means 'calf'. In an Islamic context, the significance of the name Bakkar has deep spiritual meaning, relating to both human and animal life. On one hand, human beings are often referred to as the "Khalifah" or Caliph of Allah on Earth, and the name Bakkar can be seen as a reminder to live a virtuous life, just as a calf follows its mother and grows strong and worthy. On the other hand, the name refers to the act of sacrifice, as the Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) proved his faith by preparing to sacrifice his beloved son Ismail (Ishmael), ultimately replacing him with a ram or 'Bakar'. In this sense, Bakkar is a name that inspires devotion, submission, and sacrifice in the service of Allah.
